deck.title: Little Learners (Ages 5–8): Bible Stories
deck.description: 20 read-aloud-friendly questions with 3 choices and a hint on every card.
sources: The Holy Bible, King James Version (public domain)

questions.prompt: In the very beginning, God made everything. What did God make on the first day?
questions.explanation: God said, "Let there be light," and there was light! God made light on the first day. The fish came on day five, and trees came on day three.
sources: KJV: Genesis 1:3–5 — "And God said, Let there be light: and there was light."

questions.prompt: God made the first man and woman and put them in a beautiful garden. What were their names?
questions.explanation: God formed Adam and then made Eve, and He placed them in the Garden of Eden. Mary and Joseph lived much later. They were Jesus' earthly parents.

questions.prompt: After the great flood, God put something in the sky as a promise that He would never flood the whole earth again. What was it?
questions.explanation: God set His rainbow in the clouds as a sign of His promise. Every rainbow reminds us that God keeps His word!
sources: KJV: Genesis 9:13 — "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth."

questions.prompt: How did the animals go into Noah's ark?

options.text: One at a time, all alone

questions.explanation: The animals went in two and two, male and female, just as God told Noah. (Grown-ups: Genesis 7:2 says God had Noah bring seven of some kinds of animals!)
sources: KJV: Genesis 7:9 — "There went in two and two unto Noah into the ark, the male and the female, as God had commanded Noah."

questions.prompt: Jacob gave his son Joseph a special gift that made Joseph's brothers jealous. What was it?
questions.explanation: Jacob loved Joseph and made him a coat of many colours. His brothers became jealous, but God was with Joseph the whole time.
sources: KJV: Genesis 37:3 — "...and he made him a coat of many colours."

questions.prompt: When baby Moses was in danger, his mother hid him to keep him safe. Where did she put him?

options.text: In a basket by the river

questions.explanation: Moses' mother made a little ark (basket) of bulrushes and laid him by the river. Pharaoh's daughter found him and took care of him.

questions.prompt: Young David fought a giant named Goliath. What did David use?
questions.explanation: David used a sling and one smooth stone, but he said the battle belonged to the LORD. David trusted God, not armor or swords.
questions.hint: He picked it up from a brook.

questions.prompt: Daniel was thrown into a den of lions because he kept praying to God. What happened?

options.text: God sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths

questions.explanation: God protected Daniel all night long! In the morning Daniel said God sent His angel to shut the lions' mouths.
sources: KJV: Daniel 6:22 — "My God hath sent his angel, and hath shut the lions' mouths, that they have not hurt me."

questions.prompt: Jonah ran away instead of obeying God. What swallowed Jonah?
questions.explanation: The LORD prepared a great fish to swallow Jonah. Jonah was inside the fish three days and three nights, and he prayed there. Then he obeyed God.
sources: KJV: Jonah 1:17 — "Now the LORD had prepared a great fish to swallow up Jonah."

questions.prompt: In which town was baby Jesus born?
questions.explanation: Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the city of David, and laid in a manger. Later His family went to Egypt to keep Him safe.

questions.prompt: Who followed a special star to find young Jesus and bring Him gifts?
questions.explanation: Wise men followed the star, worshipped Jesus, and gave Him gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

questions.prompt: A boy shared his lunch, and Jesus used it to feed more than 5,000 people! What was in the lunch?
questions.explanation: Jesus gave thanks for five barley loaves and two small fishes, and everyone ate until they were full. There were even twelve baskets left over!

questions.prompt: Jesus and His friends were in a boat during a scary storm. What did Jesus do?

options.text: He told everyone to swim to shore
He told the wind and waves to be still, and they obeyed

questions.explanation: Jesus said, "Peace, be still," and the storm stopped right away. Even the wind and the sea obey Him!
sources: KJV: Mark 4:37–41 — "And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm."

questions.prompt: Zacchaeus was a short man who really wanted to see Jesus. What did he do?
questions.explanation: Zacchaeus climbed a sycomore tree (that is how the KJV spells it). Jesus stopped, called him by name, and went to his house, and Zacchaeus changed his ways.

questions.prompt: In Jesus' story of the Good Samaritan, what did the Samaritan do for the hurt man?

options.text: He stopped and took care of him
He walked past on the other side

questions.explanation: Others walked by, but the Samaritan bandaged the man's wounds and paid for his care. Jesus said, "Go, and do thou likewise."

questions.prompt: In Jesus' story, a shepherd had 100 sheep and one got lost. What did the shepherd do?

options.text: Went looking until he found it

questions.explanation: The shepherd searched until he found the lost sheep and carried it home rejoicing. Jesus cares about every single person!

questions.prompt: At Easter we celebrate something wonderful. What happened three days after Jesus died?

options.text: He rose from the dead. He is alive!
He moved to a new town

questions.explanation: The angel at the tomb said Jesus had risen, just as He said. That's the happiest news ever!
sources: KJV: Matthew 28:6 — "He is not here: for he is risen, as he said."

questions.prompt: Young Samuel heard someone calling his name at night. Who was calling him?
questions.explanation: The LORD called Samuel. At first Samuel thought it was Eli, but then he answered, "Speak; for thy servant heareth."

questions.prompt: God told Joshua and the people to march around the city of Jericho. What happened when they shouted?
questions.explanation: They marched around Jericho for seven days, and when the people shouted, the wall fell down flat, just as God said.

questions.prompt: When people tried to keep children away from Jesus, what did He say?

options.text: Let the little children come to Me
Come back when you are grown up

questions.explanation: Jesus loves children! In the KJV He says, "Suffer the little children to come unto me." "Suffer" here means "let" or "allow."
sources: KJV: Mark 10:14 — "Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God."

deck.title: Kids (Ages 9–12): Bible Stories
deck.description: 20 questions from Abraham to Pentecost with KJV references.
sources: The Holy Bible, King James Version (public domain)

questions.prompt: God took Abram outside at night and made him a promise about his future family. What did God compare it to?
questions.explanation: God told Abram to look toward heaven and count the stars, and said his descendants would be that many. Abram believed God.

questions.prompt: Joseph's brothers sold him into slavery. Years later he became a ruler in Egypt and saved them from famine. What did Joseph tell his brothers?

options.text: Go home, I don't need you
You meant it for evil, but God meant it for good

questions.explanation: Joseph forgave his brothers and saw God's plan in all of it. God turned something bad into something that saved many lives.
sources: KJV: Genesis 50:20 — "But as for you, ye thought evil against me; but God meant it unto good..."

questions.prompt: How many plagues did God send on Egypt before Pharaoh let the Israelites go?
questions.explanation: There were ten plagues, from water turning to blood to the death of the firstborn. God protected Israel through the first Passover.

questions.prompt: Where did God give Moses the Ten Commandments?
questions.explanation: God gave the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai, written on tables of stone. Mount Carmel is where Elijah prayed, Ararat is where the ark rested, and the Mount of Olives is where Jesus often prayed.

questions.prompt: Pharaoh's army chased the Israelites to the edge of the Red Sea. How did God make a way?

options.text: He froze the sea into ice
He parted the waters so they walked on dry ground

questions.explanation: Moses stretched out his hand, and the LORD divided the waters. Israel walked through on dry ground!

questions.prompt: God told Gideon his army was too big, so no one could boast that they won by their own strength. How many soldiers did God use to win?
questions.explanation: Gideon started with 32,000 men, then 10,000, and God chose just 300. The victory clearly belonged to God.

questions.prompt: Samson was set apart to God as a Nazarite from birth. What part of his vow was connected to his great strength?
questions.explanation: No razor was to touch Samson's head. When he told Delilah his secret and his hair was cut, the LORD departed from him. His strength came from God.

questions.prompt: After her husband died, Ruth chose to stay with her mother-in-law, Naomi. What did Ruth promise?

options.text: I will go back to my own people
Where you go, I will go; your God will be my God
I will stay only until harvest
I will find you a home and then leave

questions.explanation: Ruth's loyal love became part of God's big plan. She became the great-grandmother of King David!
sources: KJV: Ruth 1:16 — "...whither thou goest, I will go; and where thou lodgest, I will lodge: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God."

questions.prompt: When Samuel went to choose a new king from Jesse's sons, God said He doesn't look at the outside. What does God look at?
questions.explanation: God chose David, the youngest son, a shepherd boy. People look on the outward appearance, but God looks on the heart.
sources: KJV: 1 Samuel 16:7 — "...for man looketh on the outward appearance, but the LORD looketh on the heart."

questions.prompt: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel. How did God show He is the true God?

options.text: He made it snow on the mountain
He sent fire from heaven that burned up the sacrifice, even though it was soaked with water

questions.explanation: Baal's prophets cried out all day with no answer. Elijah prayed once, and the fire of the LORD fell. The people said, "The LORD, he is the God."

questions.prompt: Queen Esther learned her people were in danger. Mordecai said she may have become queen "for such a time as this." What did Esther do?

options.text: Bravely went to the king to ask him to save her people
Wrote a letter and never spoke to the king

questions.explanation: Esther asked everyone to fast, then went to the king even though it could cost her life. She said, "If I perish, I perish." God used her to save her people.
sources: KJV: Esther 4:14 — "...who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?"

questions.prompt: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego refused to bow to the king's golden statue. What did King Nebuchadnezzar see in the fiery furnace?

options.text: The three men crying for help
The fire going out by itself
Four men walking in the fire, unhurt

questions.explanation: The king saw four men walking in the fire with no hurt! God was with them, and not even the smell of fire was on them.
sources: KJV: Daniel 3:25 — "Lo, I see four men loose, walking in the midst of the fire, and they have no hurt..."

questions.prompt: Nehemiah led the people to rebuild something broken in Jerusalem, even while enemies mocked them. What did they rebuild?
questions.explanation: The people had a mind to work and finished the wall in just 52 days. They prayed and kept building!

questions.prompt: Who baptized Jesus in the Jordan River?
questions.explanation: When John baptized Jesus, the Spirit came down like a dove, and a voice from heaven said, "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased."
questions.hint: His name is in the answer.

questions.prompt: What was Jesus' first miracle, at a wedding in Cana?
questions.explanation: John calls this the "beginning of miracles." Jesus turned water into wine when the wedding ran out.

questions.prompt: In the parable of the prodigal son, the younger son wasted his money and came home ashamed. What did the father do when he saw him coming?

options.text: Ran to him, hugged him, and threw a party

questions.explanation: The son planned to ask to be a hired servant, but the father ran to him, kissed him, and celebrated. This shows how God welcomes us back.
questions.hint: The father was full of love.

questions.prompt: Peter stepped out of the boat and walked on the water toward Jesus. Why did he start to sink?

options.text: Jesus told him to go back
He saw the strong wind and became afraid

questions.explanation: When Peter looked at the wind instead of Jesus, he got scared and began to sink. Jesus caught him and asked why he doubted.

questions.prompt: At the Last Supper, Jesus did a servant's job to teach His disciples. What did He do?
questions.explanation: Jesus washed His disciples' feet and told them to serve one another the same way.
questions.hint: It involves water and a towel.

questions.prompt: Saul was hurting Christians until something happened on the road to Damascus. What happened?

options.text: A bright light from heaven shone, and Jesus spoke to him
He fell off a camel and changed his mind
A king ordered him to stop

questions.explanation: Jesus spoke to Saul from heaven. Saul was blind for three days, then believed and became Paul, who shared the gospel everywhere.

questions.prompt: On the day of Pentecost, the disciples were together. What came upon them?

options.text: The Holy Spirit, with a sound like wind and tongues like fire

questions.explanation: The Holy Spirit filled them, and they spoke in other languages. About 3,000 people believed that day!

deck.title: Teens & Adults: Bible Stories Deep Dive
deck.description: 20 deeper questions on context, cross-references, and application.
sources: The Holy Bible, King James Version (public domain)

questions.prompt: After Cain killed Abel, God asked him where his brother was. Cain answered with a question that still challenges us today. What was it?

options.text: "Why art thou cast down, O my soul?"

questions.explanation: Cain's answer dodged responsibility. The other questions come from Pilate (John 18:38), a lawyer testing Jesus (Luke 10:29), and the psalmist (Psalm 42:5).

questions.prompt: When Abraham was tested on Mount Moriah, what did God provide in place of Isaac, and what did Abraham name the place?

options.text: A ram caught in a thicket; Jehovah-jireh ("the LORD will provide")
A lamb from a shepherd; El Shaddai

questions.explanation: God provided a ram, and Abraham named the place Jehovahjireh (KJV spelling). Jehovah-nissi was Moses' altar (Exodus 17:15), and Bethel was Jacob's naming (Genesis 28:19).
questions.hint: It was caught by its horns.

questions.prompt: After wrestling through the night, Jacob received a new name. What was it?
questions.explanation: God renamed Jacob "Israel," because he had power with God and with men and prevailed. Abram became Abraham (Genesis 17:5), and Simon was surnamed Peter (Mark 3:16).
sources: KJV: Genesis 32:28 — "Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel..."

questions.prompt: At the burning bush, Moses told God he was "slow of speech." How did God respond?

options.text: He instantly made Moses a great speaker
He told Moses to wait forty more years
He reminded Moses who made man's mouth, and appointed Aaron to speak alongside him

questions.explanation: God asked, "Who hath made man's mouth?" He promised to be with Moses and sent his brother Aaron as a spokesman. God equips the people He calls.

questions.prompt: Twelve spies explored Canaan. Ten said Israel could not win against the giants. Which two urged the people to trust God?
questions.explanation: Because the people believed the fearful report, that generation wandered forty years. Of that generation, only Joshua and Caleb entered the land.

questions.prompt: A teen is nervous about starting at a new school where she won't know anyone. Which promise God gave Joshua fits her situation best?

options.text: "Be strong and of a good courage... for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest."
"Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease."

questions.explanation: God promised Joshua His presence everywhere he went. That's the promise for new, scary places. The distractors come from Ecclesiastes 1:2, Exodus 21:24, and the rich fool in Luke 12:19.
sources: KJV: Joshua 1:9 — "Have not I commanded thee? Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest."

questions.prompt: After David's sin with Bathsheba, Nathan told a story about a rich man who took a poor man's only lamb. When David grew angry at the rich man, what did Nathan say?

options.text: "Repent ye: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand."
"Choose you this day whom ye will serve."

questions.explanation: Nathan's parable made David condemn his own sin. David confessed, and Psalm 51 records his prayer of repentance.

questions.prompt: When God told young King Solomon to ask for anything, what did Solomon request?

options.text: An understanding heart to judge the people and discern between good and bad

questions.explanation: God was pleased and gave Solomon wisdom, plus riches and honour he didn't ask for.

questions.prompt: After his victory on Mount Carmel, Elijah fled in fear and asked to die. How did God speak to him on Mount Horeb?

options.text: In a still small voice, after the wind, earthquake, and fire
In a dream about a ladder

questions.explanation: God first cared for Elijah with food and rest under the juniper tree, then spoke in a still small voice. The burning bush was Moses, and the ladder was Jacob.

questions.prompt: After Nineveh repented and God spared the city, how did Jonah react?

options.text: He moved to Nineveh to teach them
He wrote a psalm of praise
He was angry, because he knew God was gracious and merciful

questions.explanation: Jonah admitted he ran because he knew God is gracious and slow to anger. The book ends with God's question about His compassion for Nineveh.

questions.prompt: After losing his children and possessions in one day, what did Job say?

options.text: "The LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD."
"The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want."

questions.explanation: Job worshipped even in grief and did not sin or charge God foolishly. "Curse God, and die" was his wife's advice (Job 2:9), and Psalm 23 is David's.

questions.prompt: As a young captive in Babylon, Daniel "purposed in his heart" not to defile himself with the king's meat and wine. What did he ask for instead, and what happened?

options.text: Pulse (vegetables) and water; after ten days he and his friends looked healthier than the others
A forty-day fast; the king released him
Fish and honey; he was punished

questions.explanation: Daniel's respectful request became a test, and God honored his faithfulness in small daily choices.

questions.prompt: Two friends in a youth group are arguing, and a third student helps them make peace. Which Beatitude describes the helper?

options.text: "Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God."
"Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth."
"Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted."
"Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy."

questions.explanation: Peacemakers reflect their heavenly Father. The other Beatitudes (Matthew 5:4, 5, 7) are true too, but they describe different qualities.

questions.prompt: In the parable of the talents, why was the third servant rebuked?

options.text: He spent the money on himself
He gave it to the poor
He was afraid and hid his talent in the earth instead of putting it to use
He doubled it but kept it secret

questions.explanation: The faithful servants heard, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant." Faithful stewardship means using what God entrusts to us, not burying it.

questions.prompt: A lawyer asked Jesus which is the great commandment in the law. Jesus answered with two. Which pair is correct?

options.text: Keep the Sabbath; honour your father and mother
Do not steal; do not lie
Give a tenth; pray without ceasing
Love God with all your heart, soul, and mind; and love your neighbour as yourself

questions.explanation: Jesus said all the law and the prophets hang on these two commandments.
sources: KJV: Matthew 22:35–40 — "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind... Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself."

questions.prompt: Martha was busy serving while her sister Mary sat at Jesus' feet listening. When Martha complained, what did Jesus say?

options.text: "Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her."

questions.explanation: Jesus gently told Martha she was careful and troubled about many things, but one thing was needful: time with Him.

questions.prompt: Peter denied knowing Jesus three times. After the resurrection, how did Jesus restore him?

options.text: He made Peter wait a year to rejoin
He sent Peter away from the other disciples
He asked Peter three times, "Lovest thou me?" and told him to feed His sheep

questions.explanation: Three denials were answered with three chances to affirm his love, along with a new calling. That's grace in action.

questions.prompt: Two disciples walked to Emmaus with the risen Jesus but didn't recognize Him. When were their eyes opened?

options.text: When He took bread, blessed it, and broke it
When He showed them the nail prints

questions.explanation: They knew Him in the breaking of bread. Showing His hands and side happened with the disciples and Thomas (John 20:20, 27).

questions.prompt: Paul and Silas were beaten and locked in a Philippian jail. What were they doing at midnight when an earthquake opened the doors?

options.text: Praying and singing praises to God

questions.explanation: Their worship in suffering led the jailer to ask, "What must I do to be saved?" Paul answered, "Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house."

questions.prompt: Philip met an Ethiopian official reading the prophet Isaiah in his chariot. What did Philip do?

options.text: Told him to find a priest in Jerusalem
Began at that scripture and preached Jesus to him, then baptized him
Ignored him because he was a foreigner

questions.explanation: The man was reading Isaiah 53. Philip explained it points to Jesus, and the man believed and was baptized. The gospel is for every nation.
